title: Minimally invasive correction of pectus excavatum: Stabilization of the bar using pericostal sutures only – a comparative analysis of bilateral versus unilateral stabilization.
summary:
Background: After surgical repair of pectus excavatum (a sunken chest) using a minimally invasive technique called the Nuss procedure, one of the biggest problems that can occur is that the metal bar used to reshape the chest, can shift out of place. There is still no widely agreed-upon best way to keep this bar stable. 

Research Question:
Does securing the bar to the ribs using only stitches work well? And is it necessary to place these stitches on both sides of the chest, or is it just as effective to place them only on the right side?

Methodology:
After reviewing past medical records and analyzed information from 237 patients we compared two groups of patients:

Group A: Patients whose bars were stitched to the ribs on both sides

Group B: Patients whose bars were stitched only on the right side

The study looked at patient characteristics and how they did after surgery to see whether one method worked better than the other.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of patients who underwent minimally invasive correction of pectus excavatum with the Nuss technique between the years 2015 and 2024.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The patients underwent a pectus excavatum correction.
The correction was performed in the Department of Pediatric and Adolescent Surgery at the Schwarzwald-Baar Hospital between January 2015 and April 2024.
The data collected from the hospital software are sufficient for statistical analysis.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients whose collected data are not sufficient for statistical analysis
